title: Smart Collections rule document
description: One rule document per collection. This file declares the envelope every version of the format carries. The rule inside the envelope is not declared here, and one member of it is read by the validator and deliberately not declared here: "match", the member a rule is written in. The vocabulary a rule is written from is declared in the engine and written out one page each in the docs directory, the item scope arrived as the required "collects" member above, and the stages that read a composition group, a field, an operator and a value are in the validator with no member of their own in this file. That is not the coupling this sentence used to promise, and the reason is that a document declaring no "match" is accepted today: whether that is right is the question on #231, and declaring the member here would take it. A document is refused by Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Rules.RuleDocumentValidator rather than by a schema processor, so that a refusal can carry a pointer into the document and a message in the words an operator reads. This file is what an editor points at, and the suite holds it to the validator rather than to this sentence: its schemaVersion bounds, its id bounds, its name bounds, the scope member it requires and the item kinds it permits are each compared against what the engine declares, and the set of members it declares is compared against the set the validator reads in both directions, so a member that starts being read has to be declared here or named above as deliberately undeclared.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this format the document is written in. Refused when absent, because a document without one would be read as whatever shape the installed plugin happens to expect. Refused when higher than the plugin reads, because a newer version may have changed what an existing member means, and reading as far as it parses would apply a rule that means something else.

id.description: What this rule is called by everything that is not a person, and the string that is stamped on the collection the rule owns. It never changes when the name or the file changes, which is what lets a rename rename a collection instead of orphaning one. Refused when absent, because the alternatives are deriving it from the name or from the file name, and an identity derived from either changes when that one is edited. Refused when it is not a string, when it is empty, when it holds any character outside the lowercase letters a to z, the digits 0 to 9 and the hyphen, and when it is longer than the declared maximum. The set is narrow because this member is compared rather than read: an uppercase letter would make case folding decide an identity, and the rule for folding one is not the same in every language; a character outside ASCII would make a normalisation form decide it, since two encodings of one accented letter render identically and compare as different. Refusing both is what keeps two ids that look alike from being two identities wearing one face. Whitespace and control characters are outside the set and need no separate clause. The maximum is this plugin's own number rather than the server's, which declares no length for the columns a provider key and its value are stored in.

name.description: What the collection this rule owns is called, as an operator reads it in their library. It is display text and never an identity: the identity is the rule's id, so changing this member renames the collection instead of producing a second one. Refused when absent, because a create has to supply a name and the alternatives are inventing one or borrowing the file name, and the file name is the store's business rather than the operator's. Refused when it is not a string, when it is empty, when it begins or ends with whitespace, when it holds a control character, and when it is longer than the declared maximum. Edge whitespace is refused rather than trimmed because this plugin does not rewrite what an operator wrote, and two names differing only by an invisible edge are two names nobody can tell apart. Control characters are refused because the name is rendered in a web interface, where a character that displays as nothing makes the collection somebody sees a different string from the one in the document. Two rules may carry the same name deliberately: the collections they own are told apart by the stamp rather than by the title, and refusing a duplicate would make this member a second identity, which is what the id exists to prevent. The maximum is this plugin's own number rather than the server's, which declares no length for the column a collection name is stored in.

collects.description: What kinds of item this rule collects, as an array of one or more of the declared kinds. Refused when absent, because the two ways of leaving it out are both worse than refusing: defaulting to every kind makes every rule a walk over the whole library, and inferring the scope from the fields a rule happens to name makes adding one condition silently change the size of the query. Refused when it is not an array, when it is empty, when a member is not a string, when a member names no declared kind, and when a member repeats one an earlier member already named; a repeat changes nothing about what the rule collects and is left to be repaired rather than folded away, because it is most often a half-finished edit. The accepted list is this plugin's own rather than the server's enumeration: a legal set derived from a framework enumeration moves when the framework does and can be neither documented nor validated against. The order the members are written in means nothing, because a scope is a set: two documents naming one set in two orders compile to the same query. docs/rule-fields.md is where each kind is written down with what it means.
